page: OVHcloud b3-640 is a high-density, general-purpose cloud instance powered by dedicated AMD EPYC processors on the x86_64 architecture. The server features 160 physical cores with 160 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz, configured without simultaneous multithreading (one thread per physical core). Hardware resources include 640.0 GB of system RAM, providing an exact 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. Local storage is provisioned via a bundled 400 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 20 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not include GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded parallel processing efficiency. In synthetic and computational tests, the instance scored in the top tier for multi-core stress-ng operations (288,170.58), PassMark CPU score (117,207.22), Clang compilation (70,443.0), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (1,228.28 GB/sec). Memory throughput is equally robust, reaching over 9,067 GB/sec in small-block cached reads and achieving top-tier PassMark memory performance. In-memory data workloads show massive scaling, highlighted by 170.81 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations.

Per-core performance metrics align with standard-frequency server processors. Single-core evaluations, including Geekbench single-core (1912.0) and single-threaded gzip compression, place the server within the middle 50% band. Vector operations are constrained to AVX instructions, as AVX-512 and AMX instruction extensions are absent. Large-model CPU-based LLM text generation falls into lower tiers (2.32 tokens/sec on 70B models), confirming that token generation tasks require dedicated acceleration rather than pure CPU execution.

Qualitatively, the b3-640 delivers significant resource density by allocating dedicated physical cores rather than shared virtual threads. This architecture eliminates hyper-threading contention and yields predictable throughput across heavily parallelized workloads. The server fits high-capacity database systems, large-scale Redis in-memory caches, distributed compilation grids, continuous integration pipelines, batch data processing, and enterprise web-serving infrastructure.
description: OVHcloud b3-640 is a general-purpose cloud server configured with 160 dedicated AMD EPYC physical cores (160 vCPUs) clocked at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 640.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, alongside a bundled 400 GB NVMe SSD and 20 Gbps baseline networking. Without hardware GPU accelerators, the instance focuses on scalable parallel x86 compute. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-core compute and memory bandwidth, evidenced by over 288,000 in stress-ng multi-core and 170.81 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. Single-thread performance occupies mid-tier rankings due to moderate base clock speeds, and advanced extensions like AVX-512 are absent. The b3-640 is suited for large in-memory databases, continuous integration build farms, parallel batch processing, and high-concurrency web services.
